slides.texte_overlay:
5 body language mistakes that
kill your charisma in a room
Mistake 1: looking away the second someone looks at you. It reads as nervous or hiding something. Hold the look for a moment, give a small nod, then look away naturally.
Mistake 2: smiling all the time. A constant smile looks like you're asking for approval. Smile when something's actually funny or kind. A real smile means more when it's not on all night.
Mistake 3: standing too far away. Talking from two meters away feels cold. Step in to a normal distance, open your body toward the person, and the whole conversation warms up.
Mistake 4: nodding too fast while people talk. It looks like you're rushing them. Nod slowly, once in a while. It shows you're really listening and you're in no hurry.
Mistake 5: touching your neck or face when you're nervous. It's a classic stress signal everyone reads, even unconsciously. Keep your hands lower, relaxed, and you'll look calm even when you're not.
Fix the inside too. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science. When your head is full of interesting things, you're less nervous, and your body shows it.
slides.texte_sophia: I fixed my body language, then I started five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. When your head is full of interesting things, you're less nervous.

slides.texte_overlay: The fix: film yourself talking for one minute. Watch it once. You'll spot your habits instantly. Pick one to fix each week, and in a month people will notice the difference.
